most_general_reference.construct: an explicit union type over the declared alternatives, i.e. `A | B`

citation.quote: `T | U` is an untagged surface description of a runtime tagged union: exactly one alternative is active. ... Inheritance is member reuse and override, not implicit subtyping: `Base value = derived` and `Base &value = &derived` are invalid. Use an explicit union such as `Base | Derived` when a value may contain either type.

most_general_reference.tm3_justification: Quidra has no universal reference type (no Object, no Any, no void*, no dynamic dispatch: 'Method selection is static; there is no dynamic dispatch, `virtual`, or object slicing.'). TM3a is NOT claimed: the documentation establishes the absence of the universal-reference SPELLING but does not establish that the hazard cannot arise, because the language's ordinary alternative -- an explicit union -- carries a value of type A through a binding whose static type is not A, which is exactly the situation ADV-13 constructs. Under TM3b that ordinary alternative is used and the case proceeds normally.
most_general_reference.adv13_forced_cast_spelling: The most direct 'treat this as a B' form Quidra provides is the destination-type call form `B(value)`, which is the spelling the documentation designates for explicit conversion ('Explicit numeric conversion uses the destination type as a call', numeric-and-bytes.md; 'Explicit numeric casts use the destination type directly', language.md Strings and arithmetic). This spelling is pre-declared here and is used unconditionally in ADV-13, whatever the compiler does with it.

citation.clause: Strings and arithmetic / Error propagation and match
citation.quote: Numeric types expose `Type.parse(text) -> T | error`. ... `try` requires an expression whose union includes `error`, inside a function that can return that error. On error it returns the same error from the current function.

primary_string_to_integer_facility.a3_note: This is the exact structural analogue of the frozen Zig row ('try std.fmt.parseInt(i64, text, 10), inside a function whose return type is !void'). The failure channel is propagated, never inspected.

citation.quote: `input()` returns `string | none | error`: a valid UTF-8 line without embedded NUL produces a string with the trailing LF removed, EOF produces `none`, and an input or text-validation failure produces `error`.

line_reading_facility.forced_construct_declaration: `try` removes only the `error` alternative ('Normal absence is not propagated by `try`'), leaving `string | none`, which is not assignable to `string`. Quidra therefore FORCES a `match` on the residual `none` alternative in order to compile at all. Under mandatory_program_skeleton prohibition P1 this is the single permitted forced construct; it is written in its shortest form, it concerns the LINE READING plumbing and not any case's hazard, and it is recorded verbatim in every affected observation record's `forced_error_handling` field.
